objectives.text: The agencies (OCC, Federal Reserve, FDIC, NCUA) issued a joint notice of proposed rulemaking to amend requirements for supervised banks to establish, implement, and maintain effective, risk-based, and reasonably designed AML/CFT programs, aligned with concurrently proposed FinCEN changes resulting from the AML Act of 2020.

citations.quote: issued a joint notice of proposed rulemaking that would amend the requirements that each agency has issued for its supervised banks, currently referred to as Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) compliance programs, to establish, implement, and maintain effective, risk-based, and reasonably designed anti-money laundering (AML) and countering the financing of terrorism (CFT) programs
The amendments align with changes that are being concurrently proposed by the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) as a result of the Anti-Money Laundering Act of 2020 (AML Act).

objectives.text: The proposed changes would incorporate a risk assessment process requiring consideration of national AML/CFT priorities published by FinCEN, include customer due diligence requirements, codify longstanding supervisory expectations, and encourage but not require innovative approaches.

citations.quote: Incorporating a risk assessment process in AML/CFT program rules that would require, among other things, consideration of national AML/CFT priorities published by FinCEN.
Including customer due diligence requirements to reflect prior amendments to FinCEN’s requirements.
Including amendments to codify longstanding supervisory expectations and conform to changes made by the AML Act.
Encouraging, but not requiring, banks to consider, evaluate, and as appropriate, implement innovative approaches to meet compliance obligations pursuant to the BSA.

notes: This item is a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (status: horizon; evidence role: supervisory_guidance) — the obligations described are PROPOSED, not final, and are stated in conditional/would-form throughout (e.g., 'would amend', 'would require', 'The proposed rule would add'). The extracted obligations reflect the text's own hortatory/proposed framing; modalities are drawn from the described program-establishment duties but the operative force is prospective. Actual regulatory text is in the linked PDF ('Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Program Requirements (PDF)') which is not included in this source. The bulletin does not quantify thresholds. CDD/beneficial ownership and national priorities appear as coordination-layer/FinCEN cross-references per scope.
